questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.
o: much too much noisy
questions.s:
Correct Answer: too noisy

Solution:
The phrase "too much noisy" is grammatically incorrect because "too much" is used with uncountable nouns (like "water", "sugar", etc.), not adjectives.
Here, "noisy" is an adjective, so we use "too" directly before it:
✅ too noisy (correct)
❌ too much noisy (incorrect)

Correct sentence:
The place is too noisy.

Meanings:
too – excessively – बहुत ज़्यादा
noisy – full of noise – शोरगुल वाला
too much – used with uncountable nouns – बहुत ज़्यादा (अगणनीय चीजों के लिए)

questions.q: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: the planet's most ancient forest.
where researchers have unearthed
in a deserting quarry near New York,
A ground-breaking discovery has been made
questions.s:
Segment with error:in a deserting quarry near New York

Explanation:

  • The word "deserting" is incorrect in this context.

  • "Deserting" is the present participle of the verb "to desert", which means to abandon, and is not appropriate for describing a location.

  • The correct adjective should be "deserted" (meaning abandoned) or "desert-like" if referring to a dry area.

Corrected sentence:

"A ground-breaking discovery has been made in a deserted quarry near New York, where researchers have unearthed the planet's most ancient forest."

The rest of the sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.q:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

Although John trains hard, Sarah is more stronger than him, consistently lifting heavier weights at the gym during workouts.
questions.s:
In segment (b), "more stronger" is incorrect. Double Comparatives and Superlatives are to be avoided. "More" is redundant here and should be removed as "stronger" is a comparative in itself.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The corrected sentence: Although John trains hard, Sarah is stronger than him, consistently lifting heavier weights at the gym during workouts.

Note: · The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.
